target_customer: Software companies hiring engineers and engineers searching for jobs by culture; no payment model was confirmed in sources
problem: Engineers choose jobs without knowing what teams value in practice, and general job boards focus on salary and keywords rather than culture.
business_model: Job board with company profiles built from founder interviews; subscription or commission were being considered in 2017 and no revenue model is confirmed

founders.name: Lynne Tye
education: Neuroscience PhD program, dropped out (per TNW 2017)
founders.background_notes: TNW calls her a software engineer and neuroscience PhD dropout. She is the only founder listed on the YC page.

competitors.name: Indeed
competitors.what: General job search engine named by TNW as the kind of site engineers use

competitors.name: Craigslist
competitors.what: General classifieds with job listings named by TNW

technical_complexity.rationale: A content and filtering website built by one engineer. The hard part was interviewing companies to write culture profiles, not engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Any job board could add culture tags. The only edge was hand written profiles that the founder said did not scale.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source found showing incumbents copying the idea; the outcome is not documented.

market_need_then: In 2017 engineers were in short supply and the founder reported 15 inbound emails from companies in six hours after one interview, showing employer interest. No revenue was reported.

identity.voice_and_tone: Personal founder voice on the about page ('Hi, I'm Lynne')

branding.brand_signature: The name is a programming pun (key value pairs) matching the values theme; this reading is an inference from the name, not from a source
branding.community_and_virality: Founder posted on DEV Community, Hacker News and podcasts such as Software Engineering Daily in 2017, producing an engaged developer audience; no merch found.

brand_strength.rationale: Known within developer circles through founder content in 2017 but no evidence of broad recognition.

outcome_analysis: Key Values launched in 2017 as a solo founder project and joined YC in Winter 2018 with a small convertible note reported by one aggregator. It is still listed as active with one team member, so it is a small stalled or lifestyle style business rather than a venture outcome. No acquisition, shutdown or revenue information was found in public sources, and the cause of the lack of scale is not public.
notes: Company website returned HTTP 503 on two fetches (home and about), treated as unreachable at research time. CB Insights alone reports a 150K convertible note dated January 2018 with YC; unverified so not recorded as a round. Outcome search found nothing relevant. No dated competitor source beyond TNW generic boards; Rebase Now and Jobs By Culture appeared but are undated or later. TheOrg claim about Homejoy is unverified. Downgraded to depth 1: the researcher reported the branding search was not run separately for every company, so the record is redone.
